items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: Now the one thing I learned from my band director, my second band director, Alfred “Corky” Fabrizio, who still is alive and was in drum and bugle corps

ctx.x: By the way, he happened to have been a war hero believe it or not. I mean you wouldn’t think so, you know, Mr. Peepers. So now I said, “how was that.” He said, “next.” You know like, he kept going down the line, man, instead of go to the back of the line like Herman Slabonski had to go to the back of the line and start over. So now I get down to

the final table with the guys with the stamp. And I said I had to have failed, you know. He takes this stamp, I thought he was going to break the table. Bang! Fully qualified for military service. I said, “oh my God.” Here we go man. I mean even my eyes. I mean I used to wear glasses. I had 20/200 vision, a couple surgeries and cataract surgery, I’m 20/20 now you know, except I have to use reading glasses. So anyway, we get back up to Cortland, now my father owned a bar around the corner called the Crystal Hotel.…

Statue of Liberty, right where that thing I showed you there. So I had to enlist for three years in the Army, but that — and you’re guaranteed 14 months. Of course then there’s another 14 to go, that you can get a levy. You don’t get washed out, you are picked for a levy from Washington and it’s okay, somebody’s needed. So I went to basic training and as soon as I got down to Governor’s Island, Fort Jay, Governor’s Island, right across from the Statue of Liberty, the percussion leader, Sgt. Wadkowicz, he dragged…
